hints: Because the rational function is improper, use $A+B/(2x+1)+C/(x+2)$.
Clear denominators and compare the $x^2$ coefficient to find $A$.
Substitute the roots of the two linear factors to determine $B$ and $C$.
Recombine the terms to check the original numerator.
walkthrough:
Expand the denominator $(2x + 1)(x + 2) = 2x^2 + 5x + 2$. Since numerator and denominator both have degree $2$, divide the leading terms to determine the polynomial quotient $A$:
$$A = \dfrac{4x^2}{2x^2} = 2$$

Set up the partial fraction decomposition:
$$\dfrac{4x^2 + 7x + 4}{(2x + 1)(x + 2)} = 2 + \dfrac{B}{2x + 1} + \dfrac{C}{x + 2}$$

Multiply through by $(2x + 1)(x + 2)$ to form the polynomial identity:
$$4x^2 + 7x + 4 = 2(2x + 1)(x + 2) + B(x + 2) + C(2x + 1)$$

Substitute $x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ to eliminate the terms in $A$ and $C$:
$$4\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 7\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 4 = 0 + B\left(-\dfrac{1}{2} + 2\right) + 0$$
$$4\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) - \dfrac{7}{2} + 4 = \dfrac{3}{2}B$$
$$1 - \dfrac{7}{2} + 4 = \dfrac{3}{2}B \implies \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}B \implies B = 1$$

State the complete partial fraction decomposition:
$$f(x) = 2 + \dfrac{1}{2x + 1} - \dfrac{2}{x + 2}$$

hints: Integrate the decomposition from part (i), taking account of the derivative 2 in $2x+1$.
Use an antiderivative of the form $2x+\tfrac12\ln(2x+1)-2\ln(x+2)$.
Apply logarithm laws to combine the exact logarithmic terms into the stated form.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral using the partial fractions obtained in part (i):
$$\int_0^4 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_0^4 \left(2 + \dfrac{1}{2x + 1} - \dfrac{2}{x + 2}\right)\mathrm{d}x$$

Subtract the lower limit evaluation from the upper limit evaluation:
$$\int_0^4 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = (8 + \ln 3 - 2\ln 6) - (-2\ln 2) = 8 + \ln 3 - 2\ln 6 + 2\ln 2$$

Combine the logarithms using logarithm properties:
$$-2\ln 6 + 2\ln 2 = -2(\ln 6 - \ln 2) = -2\ln\left(\dfrac{6}{2}\right) = -2\ln 3$$
